summary: M.S. Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology, NY. Embedded firmware engineer in bare-metal and RTOS-based embedded C on STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontrollers, with device driver development across GPIO, timers, ADC and I2C, interrupt-driven peripheral stacks, closed-loop servo and motor actuator control, and fail-safe state machines that drive hardware to a safe state on fault.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Resolved sensor jitter via software calibration and resolution tuning, isolating where the hardware signal and the firmware's interpretation of it disagreed.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 monitoring firmware in embedded C, programming microcontroller peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with no vendor HAL.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver from the register map up.
Held a deterministic 1 Hz update rate in 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM; verified peripheral timing in Proteus before bring-up.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built RTOS firmware on STM32 using FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across tracking, actuation and display tasks.
Implemented multi-servo PWM actuator control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and a user-override path preempting autonomous tracking.

projects.name: Holonomic Drive Robot - Encoder Odometry & Closed-Loop Heading
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR), feeding angular error into rotation PWM to hold course during translation.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles as a 4-bit A/B transition state machine; drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM.
Added a fail-safe state machine halting all motor channels on controller disconnect, bringing the platform to a safe state on loss of command input.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Diagnosed and resolved 11 integration failures across the hardware/software boundary (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false positives); 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.
